sections.h2: What does the Robertson County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds records the legal papers that move title to land, including warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, deeds of trust, releases and plats. John West holds the office, which is an elected four year term, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closed on weekends.

The office's own description of its role is plain: nearly every resident makes a home or land purchase at some point, usually the largest investment of their life, so the integrity of the records matters. When a Robertson County house sells, the deed is the document that makes the transfer part of the public record, and the deed's recording is what lets the Assessor update the owner of the parcel.

sections.h2: What is the background of Robertson County, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Robertson County was organized in 1796 and named for James Robertson, the explorer who founded Nashville. Springfield, the county seat, was laid out in 1798, and tobacco was the main commodity crop through the nineteenth century into the early twentieth.

The county covers 476 square miles on the central northern edge of Tennessee, bordering Logan, Simpson and Todd counties in Kentucky, plus Sumner, Davidson, Cheatham and Montgomery counties in Tennessee. Its 2020 census population was 72,803.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Robertson County?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, quitclaim deed, deed of trust or lease costs $5.00 per page with a $10.00 minimum, plus a $2.00 electronic data processing fee. The Register's own fee of $1.00 is collected only when state tax is collected on the instrument.

Robertson County Register of Deeds recording fees
DocumentFeeSource
Deeds, deeds of trust, leases, liens, agreements$5.00 per page, $10.00 minimum, plus $2.00 processingRegister of Deeds fee page
Plat or survey map$15.00 per page plus $2.00 processingRegister of Deeds fee page
Releases$10.00 for one or two pages and one lien, $5.00 per extra page or lien, plus $2.00Register of Deeds fee page
Assignments$10.00 for one or two pages, $5.00 per extra page or assignment, plus $2.00Register of Deeds fee page
Extra instrument in one document$5.00 eachRegister of Deeds fee page

Every assignment must carry a maximum principal indebtedness statement for Tennessee recording tax purposes.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies when a Robertson County house sells?
sections.html:
The state conveyance tax is $3.70 per $1,000 of value, which is $0.37 per $100. The Register collects it under T.C.A. 67-4-409 when the deed is recorded.

Here is how that works out on a $300,000 sale: 300 multiplied by $3.70 equals $1,110 in state tax, plus the $1.00 register's fee and the page charges. A three page deed would add $15.00 and the $2.00 processing fee. The mortgage side is taxed separately at $1.15 per $1,000 of debt, with the first $2,000 exempt, so a $240,000 loan carries $273.70 in tax.

Some transfers escape the tax under the statute, including deeds between spouses that create or end a tenancy by the entirety, deeds that carry out a will, transfers into and out of a revocable living trust, and divorce settlement deeds. A quitclaim deed is taxed on actual consideration only. Ask the title company which category your deed falls in rather than assuming.

sections.h2: How do I file or search records in Robertson County?
sections.html:
You can walk a paper original into the office or send it electronically. Internet records in Robertson County go back to January 1, 1998, and the office points to ustitlesearch.com for searching them.

  • Electronic recording: accepted through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and ePN (eRecording Partners).
  • Paper filing: bring the original to the office during business hours, with the fee.
  • Name and address of the preparer: state law requires it on every document except releases and charters.
  • Drafting: have a title company or attorney prepare the deed before you bring it in.

For a full chain of title on an older parcel, a title company is the usual route.

sections.h2: What happens at the Assessor after the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Assessor of Property receives a copy of the recorded deed the next day. Moving the property into the buyer's name takes roughly 90 days, and the next tax bill goes to whoever was on file January 1.

This matters for sellers, because the bill for the current year may still carry your name after closing. The Assessor says the closing papers should state who pays that year, and the mailing address on the deed is what the office uses for the next year's notice. The Assessor's office is at 521 S. Brown St. in Springfield, 615-384-4311, and the Trustee at 515 S. Brown St., 615-384-4238, can give a payoff on any open tax.

sections.h2: What does the Robertson County housing market look like for sellers?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 28,255 households in Robertson County for 2020 to 2024, with 2.65 people per household and 89.8 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier.

  • Median monthly owner costs are $1,656 with a mortgage and $507 without one.
  • The county recorded 823 building permits in 2025.
  • The mean commute is 30.7 minutes, and 87.4 percent of households have broadband.
  • 22.4 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree, and 17.0 percent of residents are 65 or older.

Springfield is the county seat, and Adams, Cedar Hill, Cross Plains, Greenbrier and Orlinda are among the other incorporated places that file deeds through the same Register.

sections.h2: How do the Register, Assessor and Trustee fit together in a Robertson County sale?
sections.html:
Each office handles one link in the chain, and a sale touches all three in a fixed order. The deed goes to the Register first, the Assessor learns of it the following day, and the Trustee collects whatever tax is owed.

  • Before closing: ask the Trustee at 615-384-4238 for the balance on every parcel you own, since the trustee says deeds are indexed under varied spellings and a name search alone can miss one.
  • At closing: state tax and recording fees are collected by the Register when the deed is recorded, and any open tax is settled with the Trustee.
  • After closing: the Assessor updates the owner name, and the mailing address on the deed drives next year's bill.

If a bill reaches the one year delinquent mark, collection moves to Robertson County Chancery Court at 615-384-5650 and a suit is filed for the tax. Ask the Trustee which stage your bill is in before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: How can Robertson County owners protect against deed fraud?
sections.html:
The Register offers My Land Alert, a free service with free monitoring and notification, no contract and email privacy. Sign up at mylandalert.com to be told when a document is recorded against your name.

Keep the recorded copy of your deed with your closing papers so you can match the instrument number the Register assigned.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Robertson County?
faqs.a: At least $12.00. Deeds cost $5.00 per page with a $10.00 minimum, plus a $2.00 processing fee, and a $1.00 register's fee applies when state tax is collected. State tax is extra.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Robertson County, Tennessee?
faqs.a: The state conveyance tax is $3.70 per $1,000 of value, collected by the Register when the deed is recorded. Mortgages are taxed at $1.15 per $1,000 after the first $2,000.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed in Robertson County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register accepts electronic recordings through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and eRecording Partners. Paper originals are accepted at the office during business hours.

faqs.q: How far back do Robertson County online deed records go?
faqs.a: Internet records date back to January 1, 1998, searchable through ustitlesearch.com. For anything earlier, ask the Register's staff.

faqs.q: When does the new owner's name appear with the Robertson County Assessor?
faqs.a: About 90 days after the Assessor receives the recorded deed copy, which arrives the day after recording. The tax bill goes to the January 1 name until the next year.
